newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Royale Belge role at focus of attention.
newsitem.headline: Royale Belge role at focus of attention.

text.p: Belgian insurance company Royale Belge should show a marked improvement in its 1996 results on Thursday thanks mainly to extraordinary items but analysts are most interested in its strategic position.
The company with the lighthouse corporate logo is attracting a storm of interest for the first time in years.

Analysts universally agree that Royal Belge's results will be significantly better than 1995. But what the market is really looking for is clarification of its position within the newly merged French AXA-UAP group -- its main shareholder -- and its own ambitions.
Royale Belge's immediate controlling shareholder remains Royale Vendome SA, an investment vehicle 49.90 percent held by UAP and 25.10 percent by Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert(GBL).
But AXA's entry into the group structure raises questions about Royale Belge's traditional role as UAP's arm in the Benelux and, to a much lesser extent, Scandinavia, analysts said.
Some have suggested AXA-UAP could seek to raise its interest in Royale Belge and/or merge Royale Belge with AXA Belgium, perhaps combining their Dutch operations too.

Analysts are also seeking clarification about Royale Belge's stance on a "Big Belgian Bank" following support voiced this week from Generale Bank, Belgium's largest lender, for a merger with rival Banque Bruxelles Lambert.
Royale Belge owns 12.3 percent of BBL and in 1995 agreed to a BBL shareholder pact with GBL and Belgian bank Dexia CC, which both have similar sized stakes.

Some believe the pact, which is under assault from European Commission anti-trust officials and pre-dates an accord struck last year between Dexia CC and CLF-Dexia, will prove temporary. All agree BBL is "in play."

"For me there are four big issues," said Bruno de Bus of brokerage Puilaetco. "What is the attitude of AXA-UAP to Royale Belge, will they increase their stake?; what will Royale Belge do with the stake in BBL, will it increase it?; what will happen to AXA Belgium; and lastly whether Royale Belge will increase its 51 percent stake in Dutch UAP-Nieuw Rotterdam Beheer.

The consolidation of results from the Dutch unit, acquired at the end of 1995, and the consolidation for the first time for a full-year of its stake in BBL will, along with a better performance at its non-life businesses, be the main engines of growth in Royale Belge's 1996 profit, analysts said.

In addition, the bottom line will be boosted by a four billion Belgian franc capital gain -- Royale Belge's share of a deal in September to restructure the ownership of Belgian utility group Tractebel.
Excluding the capital gain, analysts pegged full-year profit in a range of 7.1 to 7.2 billion Belgian francs, up from 6.2 billion francs in 1995 and in line with the company's own forecasts.
Mignon, Hanart, Declerk analyst Stephane Rossler believed AXA-UAP would probably move to raise its stake in Royale Belge, perhaps as a prelude to a merger with AXA Belgium .

AXA Belgium chief executive officer Patrick de Courcel said last week that closer cooperation between Royale Belge, Belgium's second largest insurer, and AXA Belgium, the number six, was "the most natural scenario", adding the two groups were already studying how it could be achieved.
But analysts noted that a merger in Belgium and also closer cooperation in the Netherlands could prove difficult.

"The two businesses do not really compliment one another," said Societe Generale analyst Jean-Christian Huart. "It would create a big group but does not bring much in terms of geographic or product diversification."
